leads.candidateCapabilityName: JESD204B software-defined radio for low Earth orbit
leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Apsis Science and Technology is a Montreal engineering company that provides product-development services and is developing modular software-defined radio hardware for low-Earth-orbit communications. Apsis is developing a modular software-defined radio around the JESD204B interface so high-speed converters and mixed-signal transceivers can be selected for different low-Earth-orbit radio configurations. A Canadian Space Agency contribution agreement running from August 2025 to July 2027 supports prototype development and engineering models for Apsis's JESD204B software-defined radio.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Perceptive Space Systems is an Ontario AI and aerospace company developing space-environment intelligence for commercial, civil and defence operators. Horizon Shield is being developed to predict space-weather events and translate them into asset- and region-specific impact assessments for satellite operations, communications, navigation and critical infrastructure planning. An NRC IRAP contribution supported Horizon Shield through April 2026, while the current company site describes early-access pilots for commercial operators, launch providers and allied government programs.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Foundation Space Resources is a Calgary space-technology company developing simulation and planning tools at the intersection of aerospace and terrestrial mining. Foundation Space Resources is advancing an integrated lunar digital twin for mission planning and engineering design, including terrain, line-of-sight, lighting, shadow, space-weathering and impact-risk simulation. A Canadian Space Agency contribution running to February 2027 supports expansion of the Lunar Digital Twin's environmental models and simulation efficiency.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Quaternion Aerospace is a Victoria aerospace engineering company developing Canadian satellite platforms and modular payloads for space and uncrewed-aircraft applications. Quaternion is developing a configurable Canadian nanosatellite bus and component suite intended to reduce foreign dependence and shorten the path for domestic science, commercial and defence payloads to reach orbit. A CSA contribution runs through June 2028 for the nanosatellite platform, and a separate NRC IRAP project running through March 2027 supports a modular magnetic-anomaly-detection payload for small uncrewed aircraft.

leads.candidateCapabilityName: Low-SWaP optical amplifier for CubeSat laser communications
leads.roleSpecificEvidence: MPB Communications is a Pointe-Claire photonics company that designs and manufactures optical amplifiers, fibre lasers, sensors and payload technologies for telecommunications, space, defence and scientific applications. MPB is developing a compact optical amplification system intended to increase high-speed laser-communication capacity for CubeSats while meeting satellite size, weight, power and cost constraints. A Canadian Space Agency contribution running to June 2027 supports development and qualification of MPB's low-SWaP CubeSat optical amplifier.

leads.candidateCapabilityName: Scalium aluminum-scandium alloy for aerospace structures
leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Ferreol Technologies is a Quebec City materials company commercializing Scalium, an aluminum-scandium alloy being adapted from thin-sheet sporting applications into plates, extrusions and powders for aerospace use. Ferreol is adapting its Scalium aluminum-scandium alloy into thicker plate formats and scalable manufacturing processes for lighter aerospace and satellite components. A Canadian Space Agency contribution running through May 2028 supports scale-up, characterization and proof-of-concept work for thick Scalium plates aimed at aerospace and next-generation Canadian satellite applications.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Bubble Technology Industries is a Chalk River radiation-instrumentation company that develops and manufactures radiation and explosives-detection products for defence, aerospace, homeland security, nuclear and research applications. FlexSpec combines high-sensitivity gamma and neutron detection, isotope identification, directional localization, dynamic background compensation and GPS-tagged mapping in deployable mobile, maritime, airborne, backpack and fixed-site configurations. A current NRC IRAP contribution running to July 2027 supports continued evolution of FlexSpec radiation-detection technologies for defence and security, while a CSA project is developing a separate miniaturized ion source through December 2026.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Rocket Lab Space Systems Canada is the Toronto satellite-components operation of Rocket Lab, producing reaction wheels and star trackers and developing larger, more radiation-resilient attitude-control hardware. Rocket Lab's Toronto operation develops digitally controlled, vacuum-lubricated reaction wheels for satellite attitude control and is extending the family to higher-momentum units for medium-sized spacecraft. A Canadian Space Agency contribution running to March 2027 supports development of a higher-capacity reaction wheel for medium-sized satellite platforms at Rocket Lab's Toronto division.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Xona Space Systems Canada is a Vancouver space-navigation company developing the Canadian elements, user equipment and service operations for the Pulsar low-Earth-orbit positioning, navigation and timing system. Pulsar is a low-Earth-orbit positioning, navigation and timing architecture designed to provide stronger, authenticated signals and resilient high-precision navigation alongside existing GNSS services. Xona reports Pulsar-0 in orbit and signals under test, while its June 2026 newsroom material describes a Canadian Arctic coverage objective; the full planned constellation remains a future service rollout.

leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Orbital Research is a Burnaby satellite-communications company that designs and manufactures microwave frequency converters and related RF components for ground, airborne and space systems. Orbital's compact Ka-band up/down converter combines uplink and downlink frequency conversion in one space-qualified, software-configurable module for CubeSat and SmallSat communications payloads. Orbital publicly announced two CSA-supported converter projects in March 2025, and its current product catalogue lists the resulting space-rated Ka-band up/down-converter family.
